KEY MESSAGE 1...Mix of clouds and sun with off-and-on showers 
through the afternoon, with decreasing clouds and a cool evening 
tonight. Full sun, seasonable temperatures and low humidity for 
the Labor Day Monday holiday.

We're still governed by broad cyclonic flow aloft around a closed 
mid/upper low over Nova Scotia, a feature which has moved very 
little over the last 24 hours. This has led to a mix of clouds and 
sun, and some heating where clouds have scattered has led to 
"destructive sunshine" which has blossomed additional cloudiness 
with scattered pop-up showers moving southward. These clouds and 
scattered showers will continue through sundown. An additional 
shortwave and mid-level moisture move southward from coastal ME 
could sustain cloud cover across eastern New England for a few hours 
after sundown, but we should trend mostly clear with falling 
dewpoints overnight supporting good radiational cooling. There could 
be some patchy mist or fog developing around sunrise, especially in 
those areas which received rain. We also have one final evening with 
nuisance splashover around the early-evening high tide at Nantucket 
and the Cape and Islands with coastal flood advisories still in
effect. We fell just short of Advisory criterion last night at 
Nantucket at 4.91 ft, and tonight should end up being similar 
with a higher high-tide but weaker northerly winds. Lows tonight
should dip into the mid to upper 40s in the favored radiational
cooling locations, and in the low to mid 50s elsewhere, warmest
lows Cape and Islands. 

Rising 500 mb heights on Labor Day Monday support full sun and 
temperatures warming back into the mid to upper 70s, with low 
humidity levels (dewpoints in the 40s to low 50s!) with some 
northwesterly winds around 10 mph. Overall about as ideal weather 
conditions for outdoor activities as one could ask for. By Monday 
evening, clear skies early favoring strong radiational cooling then 
give way to increasing midlevel cloud cover from the northwest by 
the pre-dawn hours as a strong shortwave disturbance aloft passes to 
our northeast. Lows end up slightly warmer, in the to mid 50s for 
most, with mid/upper 50s for the eastern and southern coastlines. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Dry conditions Tuesday through much of 
Wednesday. Pattern becomes more unsettled later Wednesday into 
early Friday with periods of showers possible. 

On Tuesday, the deeper mid-level trough continues to shift further 
eastward as a mid-level ridge continues to build in from the west. 
925mb temperatures warm to +17-18C yielding high temperatures in the 
upper 70s with locations potentially hitting the 80 degree mark in 
the valleys. High pressure in place will support mainly dry 
conditions.  

Ensemble guidance shows a signal for a transition to a more 
unsettled pattern mid to late week. The mid-level ridge begins to 
break down Wednesday, becoming more zonal by Thursday. Ensemble 
guidance shows a consensus with a series of shortwave troughs moving 
through the flow later Wednesday through Friday. This should be 
accompanied by a plume of above normal moisture, rising to 160-190% 
of normal by early Thursday yielding PWATS of 1.5" approaching 2.0". 
The positioning of an upper jet should supply ascent for periods of 
showers. There is spread across guidance in the finer details of the 
timing of the waves which will influence timing of the showers. A 
shortwave pushes through sometime Wednesday evening/night triggering 
the first round of showers which should taper off through the 
morning Thursday (at latest). The next wave moves through late 
Thursday/Thursday Night bringing another round of showers. With the 
timing of the waves still variable across guidance this leaves some 
uncertainty in thunderstorm/downpour potential. There will be plenty 
of moisture to support downpours; however, the timing of the wave 
would need be early enough to tap into the marginal instability 
build through the day for convection. Something to keep monitoring. 
For now, we are not seeing a strong signal for severe or flash 
flooding, just periods of showers with generally light accumulations 
(< 0.60"). 

An 850mb 35-45kt LLJ shifts across southern New England into 
Thursday. There does raise a flag for potentially gustier winds; 
however, this will come down to how well we can mix down from 850mb 
or even 925mb. If things align, ensembles show potential for gusts 
in the 20-35 mph range on Thursday across the land and coastal 
waters. Still plenty of details to work out in the pattern before we 
come into better agreement about the gusts, but something to watch 
for now.  

Temperatures Wednesday/Thursday lean near to slightly above normal 
with temperatures in the mid to upper 70s. A cold front pushes 
through early Friday bringing a cooler airmass this will support 
highs in the upper 60s low 70s.
